title: Homotopies for Roos comparison maps
statement: In an abelian category with countable products [def-sp-abelian], let I,J be integer complexes of towers [def-weil-inverse-system], with chain maps u:I\to J and r:J\to I and a homotopy ur\sim id_I [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Choose termwise-product complexes P,PJ, termwise kernels L,LJ of their transition endomorphisms [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism], and signed cones C,CJ with differential (y,x)\mapsto(-dy-sx,dx). Given lU,cU,lR,cR whose components are the induced kernel and diagonal cone maps of Pi.map(u) and Pi.map(r) under these presentations (the four component equations in lean.statement), there are homotopies lU lR\sim id_L and cU cR\sim id_C. No comparison map eta, splitting or K-injectivity is assumed.

proof.text: Conjugate the product of each component of hr through eP to obtain H_pq. The product homotopy equation gives U R - id = d H + H d. Naturality of hr with the transitions gives s_p H_pq=H_pq s_q.

Factor iota_p H_pq through the limiting kernel fork hL_q and set nonadjacent components zero. Compose the homotopy equation with the monomorphism iota_p. The specified components of lU,lR reduce it to the product equation, giving the kernel homotopy.

Under eC define the cone homotopy in degree p+1 to be diag(-H_(p,p-1),H_(p+1,p)). The four component hypotheses identify the composites with the diagonal product of U R. Matrix multiplication with the signed cone differential gives the two diagonal homotopy equations; the off-diagonal term -s_(p+1) H_(p+1,p)+H_(p+1,p) s_p vanishes. The remaining degrees vanish by shape.

lean.statement:
theorem roos_comparison_homotopies
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [HasLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) A]
    (I J : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ)
    (u : I ⟶ J) (r : J ⟶ I) (hr : Homotopy (u ≫ r) (𝟙 I))
    (P L C : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (eP : ∀ p : ℤ, P.X p ≅ ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (I.X p).obj (Opposite.op n)))
    (hP : ∀ p q : ℤ, P.d p q ≫ (eP q).hom =
      (eP p).hom ≫ Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (I.d p q).app (Opposite.op n)))
    (oneSubS : P ⟶ P)
    (hS : ∀ p : ℤ, oneSubS.f p = (eP p).hom ≫
      towerTransitionEndomorphism
        (fun n ↦ (I.X p).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ≫ (eP p).inv)
    (iota : L ⟶ P)
    (hKernel : ∀ p : ℤ, iota.f p ≫ oneSubS.f p = 0)
    (hL : ∀ p : ℤ, IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (iota.f p) (hKernel p)))
    (eC : ∀ p : ℤ, C.X (p + 1) ≅ P.X p ⊞ P.X (p + 1))
    (hC : ∀ p : ℤ, C.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1) ≫ (eC (p + 1)).hom =
      (eC p).hom ≫ biprod.lift
        (-(biprod.fst ≫ P.d p (p + 1)) - biprod.snd ≫ oneSubS.f (p + 1))
        (biprod.snd ≫ P.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1)))
    (PJ LJ CJ : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (ePJ : ∀ p : ℤ, PJ.X p ≅ ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (J.X p).obj (Opposite.op n)))
    (hPJ : ∀ p q : ℤ, PJ.d p q ≫ (ePJ q).hom =
      (ePJ p).hom ≫ Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (J.d p q).app (Opposite.op n)))
    (sJ : PJ ⟶ PJ)
    (hSJ : ∀ p : ℤ, sJ.f p = (ePJ p).hom ≫
      towerTransitionEndomorphism
        (fun n ↦ (J.X p).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ≫ (ePJ p).inv)
    (iJ : LJ ⟶ PJ)
    (hKJ : ∀ p : ℤ, iJ.f p ≫ sJ.f p = 0)
    (hLJ : ∀ p : ℤ, IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (iJ.f p) (hKJ p)))
    (eCJ : ∀ p : ℤ, CJ.X (p + 1) ≅ PJ.X p ⊞ PJ.X (p + 1))
    (hCJ : ∀ p : ℤ, CJ.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1) ≫ (eCJ (p + 1)).hom =
      (eCJ p).hom ≫ biprod.lift
        (-(biprod.fst ≫ PJ.d p (p + 1)) - biprod.snd ≫ sJ.f (p + 1))
        (biprod.snd ≫ PJ.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1)))
    (lU : L ⟶ LJ) (cU : C ⟶ CJ) (lR : LJ ⟶ L) (cR : CJ ⟶ C)
    (hlU : ∀ p : ℤ, lU.f p ≫ iJ.f p = iota.f p ≫ (eP p).hom ≫
      Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (u.f p).app (Opposite.op n)) ≫ (ePJ p).inv)
    (hcU : ∀ p : ℤ, cU.f (p + 1) ≫ (eCJ p).hom = (eC p).hom ≫ biprod.map
      ((eP p).hom ≫ Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (u.f p).app (Opposite.op n)) ≫ (ePJ p).inv)
      ((eP (p + 1)).hom ≫
        Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (u.f (p + 1)).app (Opposite.op n)) ≫ (ePJ (p + 1)).inv))
    (hlR : ∀ p : ℤ, lR.f p ≫ iota.f p = iJ.f p ≫ (ePJ p).hom ≫
      Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (r.f p).app (Opposite.op n)) ≫ (eP p).inv)
    (hcR : ∀ p : ℤ, cR.f (p + 1) ≫ (eC p).hom = (eCJ p).hom ≫ biprod.map
      ((ePJ p).hom ≫ Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (r.f p).app (Opposite.op n)) ≫ (eP p).inv)
      ((ePJ (p + 1)).hom ≫
        Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (r.f (p + 1)).app (Opposite.op n)) ≫ (eP (p + 1)).inv))
    : Nonempty (Homotopy (lU ≫ lR) (𝟙 L)) ∧
      Nonempty (Homotopy (cU ≫ cR) (𝟙 C))
